title: Credit card pre-authorisation: why you may not see a refund
description: Understand credit card pre-authorisation (pre-auth), why releasing a pending hold usually creates no refund transaction, and what to check in your banking app.
intro: Seeing an amount disappear from your available balance can feel like you have been charged. It is understandable to look for a refund afterwards. If the amount was only a credit card pre-authorisation (pre-auth) hold and was never charged, its release usually works differently: the pending hold disappears, rather than a separate refund arriving.

sections.heading: The short answer: check Pending, not just Refunds
sections.html:
If your security amount was held but never charged, you will usually not see a separate refund transaction when it is released. Instead, look for the original amount under Pending in your banking app. After your bank processes the release, that pending hold will usually disappear and the held amount becomes available to spend again.

Some banks keep a record marked “reversed”, “cancelled” or similar. The exact display depends on your bank. Check that the pending item has not changed into a completed charge.

sections.heading: What is a credit card pre-authorisation (pre-auth)?
sections.html:
A credit card pre-authorisation, often shortened to pre-auth or called a security hold, temporarily reserves an amount on your card. Think of it as money set aside, rather than money paid to ProHouse.

For a hold that has not been captured as a payment, the held amount has not been transferred to ProHouse. However, you cannot spend that amount while it is reserved. On a debit card this reduces your available funds; on a credit card it reduces your available credit.

sections.heading: Why does it look like money has been taken?
sections.html:
Banking apps often show a hold as a negative amount alongside other transactions. Your available balance or available credit also falls. That can look like a payment even though the transaction is still pending.

Example only: if you have $1,000 available and a $200 hold is placed, you may see $800 available. If the full hold is released without any payment being taken, the $200 becomes available again once your bank updates it. You would not normally see an extra $200 refund entry. This example is not ProHouse’s required security amount.

sections.heading: Release of a hold versus refund of a payment
sections.html:
• Hold released: an amount was reserved but not charged. The reservation is removed. A separate refund entry is usually not created.
  • Payment refunded: an amount was actually charged and is then returned. Your bank may show a refund credit or reverse the original payment.
  • Hold captured: some or all of the reserved amount becomes a completed payment. This is different from simply releasing the full hold.

This guide describes an uncaptured security hold, not your accommodation payment. If an amount has become a completed charge, ask us to check that specific transaction rather than assuming it is a released hold.

sections.heading: How to check your banking app
sections.html:
1. Open the card account used for the security pre-auth.
  2. Find the original amount and date in the Pending or authorisations section.
  3. After the release is processed, check whether the hold has disappeared or is marked reversed/cancelled.
  4. Check your available balance or available credit, allowing for other spending and pending transactions.
  5. If the entry has become completed or posted, contact ProHouse so we can check whether a payment was taken.

The disappearance of a pending entry alone does not prove that it was released: it can also disappear when replaced by a completed payment. Check both sections.

sections.heading: Still seeing the hold? Here is what to ask
sections.html:
A release by a business and an update in your banking app may not happen at the same time. Processing depends on your bank, card and transaction; there is no single release time for every guest.

Contact ProHouse if you need us to confirm the pre-auth status for your booking. If we have confirmed release but your available funds have not updated, ask your bank: “Is this a pending pre-auth hold or a completed payment, and when will the released hold stop affecting my available balance?”

You can send us your booking reference, transaction date and amount. If sharing a screenshot, hide your full card/account numbers and unrelated transactions. Never send your card security code, online banking password or one-time passcodes. Contact ProHouse if you would like help checking.

title: Private room or whole apartment for your Sydney short stay?
description: Compare privacy, shared spaces, bathrooms and total booking costs before choosing a private room or whole apartment for a Sydney short stay.
intro: Two listings can show a similar bedroom photograph while offering very different stays. Before comparing prices, establish whether you are booking one room or exclusive use of an apartment. That choice affects privacy, shared facilities and how comfortably the space fits your trip.

sections.heading: Start with what is exclusively yours
sections.html:
A private-room booking gives you the bedroom described in the listing. Other spaces may be shared with other guests. A whole-apartment booking gives you exclusive use of the apartment described in that particular listing; it does not mean exclusive use of the building or its common facilities.

At ProHouse’s Wolli Creek shared apartment, private-room guests have their own bedroom and ensuite, while the kitchen and living room are shared. Check the Room 1, Room 2 and Room 3 pages and your selected booking details for the exact room.

sections.heading: Compare the bathroom as carefully as the bed
sections.html:
“Private room” alone does not tell you whether the bathroom is shared, dedicated or directly connected to the bedroom. Look for the bathroom description, room photographs and any access arrangements. If the wording is unclear, ask before booking.

For a group, also check the number of bathrooms and sleeping arrangements. A room’s capacity is the capacity of that booking, not permission to use the other bedrooms in a shared apartment.

sections.heading: Think about how you will use the shared areas
sections.html:
A shared kitchen can suit a guest who wants to prepare breakfast or a simple meal. It also requires consideration: clear up after cooking, leave space for others and follow the property’s quiet-hours rules. A shared living room is available to other guests too.

If your trip depends on having a lounge, kitchen and several bedrooms entirely to your group, compare whole-apartment options rather than assuming those areas come exclusively with a private room.

sections.heading: Compare the total for the same trip
sections.html:
Use the same dates, guest count and length of stay for each option. Check the final price, cleaning charges, parking arrangements and cancellation conditions. A security pre-authorisation, where required, should be understood separately from the accommodation price.

For a short airport stopover, the arrival process may matter as much as the room. A self check-in property still requires you to complete its preparation steps. Read our self check-in checklist before travelling.

sections.heading: A quick decision checklist
sections.html:
• Is the booking for a room or the whole apartment?
  • Is the bathroom an ensuite, dedicated bathroom or shared bathroom?
  • Which kitchen and living areas are shared?
  • Does the exact bed setup suit every booked guest?
  • Can you complete the arrival requirements before your trip?
  • Have you compared the final price and cancellation conditions?

Choose the space that fits how you will actually stay. You can compare ProHouse stays and then check availability for your dates.

title: A self check-in checklist for your Sydney short stay
description: Prepare your arrival link, identity verification, access instructions and support details before travelling to a self check-in short stay in Sydney.
intro: Self check-in gives you a way to arrive without collecting a key at a reception desk. A smooth arrival begins before you travel: finish the required checks, understand when access becomes available and keep the correct instructions close at hand.

sections.heading: Before booking: check whether the arrival process suits your trip
sections.html:
Read the property’s check-in time, approval hours and support arrangements. An accommodation business can offer self check-in while having limited staff support outside office hours. Do not assume there is an onsite reception or that an unfinished verification can be approved late at night.

ProHouse uses self check-in with no onsite reception. Arrival approvals take place Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm. If you are travelling outside that window, complete the required preparation in advance. Check the airport accommodation page and the instructions sent for your booking.

sections.heading: Before travelling: finish the required steps
sections.html:
Find your pre-arrival email and use its link to complete identity verification, provide your estimated arrival time and finish the required security-deposit steps. Completing a form and receiving approval are different stages; check the status shown for your own booking.

Use the contact details on the official ProHouse website if something is unclear. Avoid putting identity documents or payment details into an unfamiliar link sent by someone claiming to represent the property.

sections.heading: Save the link, not a guessed door code
sections.html:
Keep the same arrival link available on your phone. For ProHouse, access details are released through that link from 3pm on arrival day after the required steps are completed. An empty access section before release time does not necessarily mean something has gone wrong.

Read the full route from the street entrance to your booked room. Building access, a lockbox and a room lock may be separate steps. A map pin or building name alone may not identify the correct guest entrance.

sections.heading: Check your phone and your parking plan
sections.html:
• Charge your phone and keep a way to access your arrival email.
  • Confirm the exact booked address and room.
  • Check the arrival time and when your access details become available.
  • Arrange any required parking before relying on it.
  • Save the property’s official contact information.
  • Read the instructions before you reach the entrance.

Keep access links and codes private. Do not share them publicly or use another guest’s instructions. Parking arrangements are separate from bedroom access; follow the information provided for your own booking.

sections.heading: If you need help on arrival
sections.html:
Check that you are using the right entrance, your own booking link and the instructions for the current stay. Contact the property with a clear description of the step that is not working. Do not send a door code in a public message or review.

ProHouse support outside business hours is limited. Follow the emergency and contact instructions in your arrival information rather than assuming immediate assistance is available. If you have not booked yet, ask about the arrival process before choosing your dates.

title: What to check when choosing accommodation near Sydney Airport
description: Compare terminal access, room type, arrival requirements and total costs when choosing accommodation near Sydney Airport and Wolli Creek.
intro: “Near Sydney Airport” is a useful starting point, but it does not describe the whole journey. The right choice depends on your terminal, transport, arrival time and the kind of accommodation you want. Use these questions to compare your options before booking.

sections.heading: Plan the trip to your terminal
sections.html:
Check which terminal your airline uses and plan the journey from the accommodation’s actual address. A short distance on a map is not the same as a confirmed walking route, train connection or taxi journey. Allow for luggage, waiting and your airline’s check-in requirements.

Use the Transport for NSW trip planner for a journey at the time you expect to travel. Check current fares and services directly rather than relying on an old blog’s exact travel-time estimate.

sections.heading: Choose the accommodation type deliberately
sections.html:
A hotel, a private room in a shared apartment and a whole apartment can all serve an airport trip, but their facilities and service models differ. Check whether reception is onsite, whether common areas are shared and what bathroom arrangement is included.

ProHouse’s Wolli Creek private-room accommodation is in a shared apartment, with private bedrooms and ensuites plus a shared kitchen and living room. It is outside the airport terminals and has no onsite reception. Read our room-versus-apartment guide if you are deciding between booking types.

sections.heading: Match the arrival requirements to your flight
sections.html:
For an early arrival, establish when the room will actually be available. For a late arrival, check whether any identity verification or payment steps need staff approval beforehand. Do not assume self check-in means you can finish every administrative step at any hour.

At ProHouse, check-in starts from 3pm after the required arrival preparation. Approval hours are Monday–Friday, 9am–5pm. Complete the process before travelling, especially when your journey falls outside those hours. Our self check-in checklist explains what to prepare.

sections.heading: Compare the complete stay cost
sections.html:
Compare the same dates and number of guests. Review the final accommodation total, any cleaning charges, transport costs and parking conditions. If driving, check whether parking must be booked separately and whether your vehicle suits the available space.

Read the cancellation conditions that apply to the selected rate. A cheaper room may have different flexibility, while a longer stay can change the importance of kitchen access and shared facilities. Avoid choosing on a headline nightly price alone.

sections.heading: Make the booking easy to follow
sections.html:
Before paying, check the exact room, address, guest capacity and arrival process. Keep the booking confirmation and official contact details together. If staying near Wolli Creek is suitable for your trip, explore ProHouse’s airport accommodation information and check the room details for your dates.

For a city visit as well as a flight, review the Wolli Creek location guide and plan each journey separately. Your best airport base is the one that fits the full trip, not only the nearest-looking map pin.

title: Questions to ask a short-stay property manager before you sign
description: Compare short-stay property management scope, commission, property costs, guest access, maintenance and owner reporting before choosing a manager.
intro: A management commission is only one part of choosing someone to look after your property. A useful comparison sets out who does each job, what it costs and how you will know what is happening. Take these questions into your first conversation with a short-stay manager.

sections.heading: What is included in the management fee?
sections.html:
Ask for a written description of the service. Discuss listing preparation, booking channels, guest communication, arrival arrangements, pricing, cleaning coordination and maintenance reporting. Establish which tasks the manager handles directly and which involve separate suppliers.

For any quoted percentage, ask what amount it is calculated on, whether tax is included and which costs are additional. Compare a realistic example that separates accommodation income, commission, platform costs, cleaning and other agreed expenses. This makes competing proposals easier to understand.

sections.heading: Who pays to get the apartment ready?
sections.html:
Walk through photography, furniture, linen, kitchen equipment and access setup before a launch date is promised. Clarify who chooses items, who approves purchases and who owns them. An onboarding service and the physical items purchased for a property are different costs.

Ask the manager to identify what is essential for opening and what can wait. Agree the scope and budget for your particular home rather than assuming a package covers every expense. ProHouse describes its current approach on the List your home page; confirm the applicable proposal directly.

sections.heading: How will guests arrive and get support?
sections.html:
Ask how guests receive arrival instructions, when access becomes valid and how access ends after a stay. Discuss the backup plan for a lock problem, who receives maintenance reports and how urgent issues are escalated. Keep security details out of public listings.

Also ask about support hours and the difference between emergency assistance and routine enquiries. Clear expectations help you judge whether the service model suits the property and the guests you want to host.

sections.heading: How are cleaning and maintenance decisions handled?
sections.html:
Agree who checks the property between bookings, how problems are documented and when an owner is contacted. Discuss purchase approval limits, supplier invoices and what happens when work cannot wait. Ask how maintenance responsibilities involving the building or strata are identified and escalated.

Before committing, confirm which approvals, insurance arrangements and property-specific requirements need checking with the relevant authority, insurer or adviser. A manager’s marketing proposal alone should not be treated as confirmation that every home is suitable for short stays.

sections.heading: What will I see in my owner reporting?
sections.html:
Ask for an example of the owner statement and how booking income, deductions and payments are explained. Discuss how pricing decisions are reviewed and what data will be available. Treat any income forecast as an estimate with assumptions, not a guaranteed return.

Finally, read the agreement’s provisions for owner use, rate changes, ending the arrangement and transferring listing or access information. Put important answers in the written agreement. To start a ProHouse conversation, tell us about your home, its suburb, bedrooms and current setup.
